name: Sotol

facts.where: West Texas hills and Big Bend country

caution: Only the cooked heart is food, and preparing it is a serious pit-roasting project, not a trail snack. The leaves are saw-toothed. Never eat a wild plant on this guide's word alone. Confirm identity against several sources and learn the look-alikes first.

sections.title: Identification
sections.body: A rosette of slender saw-edged leaves sending up a tall flower stalk, also called desert spoon. A signature plant of the Trans-Pecos.

sections.title: Uses
sections.body: Indigenous peoples pit-roasted the hearts for days into a sweet food, and the same plant is distilled into the spirit sotol.
